planeFitToCameraTool.title: Plane Fit To Camera Tool
planeFitToCameraTool.copy: A Unity editor tool for aligning one or more Plane objects to the camera view. It is useful when you need a full-screen panel, background layer, overlay surface, or screen-space effect without switching to a Canvas workflow.

cards.title: Best For
cards.body: Background cards, full-screen overlays, screen shaders, and VRChat gimmick setups that need a plane to match the camera frame precisely.

cards.title: Camera Support
cards.body: Works with both perspective and orthographic cameras, using the correct sizing logic for each camera mode.

cards.title: Workflow
cards.body: You can register multiple Plane objects, control distance and rotation options, and fit them in one pass to reduce repetitive setup work.

cards.title: Editor Only
cards.body: This is an editor-only tool that does not add runtime components. It is designed for fast scene-side plane alignment work during setup and presentation staging.

meta.body: The tool is optimized for the default Unity Plane (XZ, 10×10) and also works with XZ-based meshes that behave like planes.

image.alt: Plane Fit To Camera Tool English UI screenshot
image.caption: The editor window lets you assign a camera, manage multiple planes, and apply distance and rotation options before running Fit Plane(s).

sections.title: Key Features
items: Automatically aligns Plane scale, position, and rotation to the active camera frame.
Supports both perspective cameras (FOV-based) and orthographic cameras (orthographicSize-based).
Allows multiple Plane objects to be registered and fitted in one operation.
Optimized for the default Unity Plane (XZ, 10×10), while still supporting similar XZ-based meshes.
Supports both current-distance usage and manual distance input.
Includes a square mode for forcing width and height to match.
Includes Korean, English, and Japanese UI plus full Unity Undo support.

sections.title: Requirements
items: A Unity Plane or a comparable XZ-oriented mesh

sections.title: Basic Usage
items: Open Studio Iyan > Tools > Plane Fit To Camera from the Unity menu.
Assign the target camera in the Camera field.
Add one or more Plane objects to the plane list.
Configure Align Position, Align Rotation, Distance, Keep Square, and Image Rotation as needed.
Click Fit Plane(s) to align the registered planes to the camera view.

entries.title: Align Position
entries.body: Moves the Plane to camera.position + camera.forward * distance so it sits at the target depth in front of the camera.

entries.title: Align Rotation
entries.body: Rotates the Plane so its facing direction matches the camera, then applies the extra orientation needed to fill the screen correctly.

entries.title: Use Current Distance / Manual Distance
entries.body: You can project the current object position onto the camera forward axis, or override it with a manual distance value. If the object is behind the camera, the tool falls back to the manual distance.

entries.title: Keep Square (Width = Height)
entries.body: Uses the larger of the computed width or height and applies it to both axes to create a square result.

entries.title: Image Rotation / Language
entries.body: Image Rotation spins the Plane around the camera-facing axis using 0° / 90° / 180° / 270° steps. The window also lets you switch the UI language between Korean, English, and Japanese.

sections.title: Tips and Use Cases
items: For a fixed background, parent the Plane to the camera, then run Fit Plane(s) once before final placement.
If you use a custom mesh, it will still be treated like an XZ plane by default and can be adjusted manually afterward if needed.
Good use cases include flat color backgrounds, gradient panels, screen-shader surfaces, cutscene panels, and VRChat screen effects.

entries.title: The Plane does not fully fill the screen
entries.body: Make sure the camera used in the Game view matches the camera assigned in the tool. If you changed the FOV or aspect ratio, run Fit Plane(s) again.

entries.title: The texture looks upside down or sideways
entries.body: Try the Image Rotation options first. If the issue remains, verify the UV orientation of the mesh itself.

entries.title: The Plane appears behind other objects
entries.body: Increase Manual Distance to move it farther forward, and check Render Queue, ZWrite, or ZTest settings if the material still renders behind something else.

entries.title: Nothing happens when Fit Plane(s) is clicked
entries.body: Confirm that both a Camera and at least one Plane entry are assigned. It is also worth checking the Console for warnings such as missing MeshFilter or sharedMesh references.
